00334.label: Concurrent daily temozolomide with radiotherapy

medicines.name: Oral 5-HT3 antagonist - select ONE
medicines.dose: Ondansetron 8-16 mg total daily OR granisetron 1-2 mg total daily; prescriber selects and records agent/dose
medicines.timing: Daily during the concurrent temozolomide course, including non-radiotherapy days; confirm the written stop date
medicines.note: NCCP V6 Table 5, p8. Start at least 30 minutes before oral SACT (p4). Confirm stop date, delayed-emesis cover and rescue plan; review QT risk, liver function, constipation and interactions.

medicines.name: PJP prevention
medicines.dose: Complete the local prophylactic agent, dose and schedule
medicines.timing: Required throughout concurrent temozolomide/radiotherapy; review continuation after RT
medicines.note: Continue when clinically indicated for lymphopenia/steroid exposure. Do not stop automatically at the end of RT; confirm allergy, renal function, interactions and pharmacy plan.

additional_support: Temozolomide has moderate-to-high oral emetic potential. Take the prescribed anti-sickness plan before chemotherapy and use rescue medicine as instructed. Ask what to do if nausea prevents taking medicines or fluids.

PJP-prevention medicine is required during temozolomide with radiotherapy in this NCCP regimen. Your team supplies the prescription and decides how long to continue, including if lymphocyte counts remain low. Do not stop it just because radiotherapy has finished.

Anti-sickness medicines and other medicines can worsen constipation. Ask for your bowel plan, and call for persistent vomiting, severe constipation or difficulty drinking. Do not double a dose after vomiting.

Keep steroids and seizure medicines on their own written schedules if prescribed. They are not routine medicines for every patient, and chemotherapy rest days do not automatically mean stopping them. Ask the pharmacist to check interactions.

These are prescription choices for clinician/pharmacist completion, not an issued prescription. General NCCP multiday guidance includes cover after the last SACT day; record the individual duration. Review pre-existing steroid and seizure treatment rather than duplicating it.
